code.title: Listen to eight events on two chains
code.lead: The reactive contract is wired once. After that, a matching log on any of the three contracts calls react().

notes.text: One-time wiring. The owner can call this once and has no other power over the system.
Subscribes to the price feed's AnswerUpdated on Base.
Each destination is confirmed by an event, so a loan is only final when the other chain says so.
Reactive Omni's system contract. Subscribing from a function, not the constructor, works: the vault and pool need this contract's address first.

code.title: One entry point for every event
code.lead: Reactive calls react() with the log. The contract checks which chain and which contract it came from before doing anything.

notes.text: Only Reactive's system contract can call this.
A look-alike contract emitting the same event is ignored: the chain id and the exact address are checked.
A new price. This is where unhealthy loans are found.
A new loan. The size, the loan count and the LTV are checked here, at the price Reactive last saw.
The debt chain confirmed the liquidation. Only now is the seize requested.

code.title: Find unhealthy loans, ask Unichain to close them
code.lead: On every price update the reactive contract walks its open loans and sends one callback per loan that crossed 80%.

notes.text: Replayed or out-of-order rounds are ignored.
At most 10 liquidations per update, so one reactive transaction stays under the 900k gas cap.
Marks the loan Liquidating and requests liquidate() on Unichain.
The callback. Unichain's proxy accepts it only from this contract, and the first argument is replaced with this contract's address.

code.title: Only Reactive can move the collateral
code.lead: The vault holds the borrower's tWETH. It has no owner key that can seize it.

notes.text: The caller must be Base's callback proxy.
The proxy reports which reactive contract sent it. Anyone else is rejected.
Idempotent: a duplicate or late callback does nothing, so retries are safe.
Frees one of the borrower's three loan slots.
Whatever collateral is left after debt plus the 5% penalty goes back to the borrower.

code.title: The debt chain closes first
code.lead: Repay and liquidate both change the loan's state on Unichain, so exactly one of them can win.

notes.text: After liquidate() lands, repay() on that loan reverts. A borrower can never repay and also lose the collateral.
State is set before the transfer.
The seize on Base only follows after Reactive sees this event.

code.title: Anyone can unstick a loan
code.lead: A callback can fail, for instance if a destination runs out of callback funds. No keeper is needed to recover.

notes.text: Only after a minute without an answer, so it cannot be used to spam.
Re-sends the pending step. The callbacks are idempotent, so a duplicate does nothing.
Healthy and finished loans are left alone.

code.title: Spam costs the operator, so it is limited
code.lead: Every price update makes the reactive contract run once, and the operator pays for each run.

notes.text: One update per 30 seconds from anyone, which caps the spam at two reactions a minute.
An update that changes nothing would only cost a reaction.
No more than a 50% move per update.
The same event Chainlink's aggregators emit, so a real feed could replace this one.
